newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares inch into positive territory at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares inch into positive territory at close.

text.p: * Shares overcome impact of ex-divs to end level
* Telecom, Fletcher Building firm, Hallenstein tumbles
* Some selling seen if Labour-led govt announced
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
339 +5 * NZSC cap index -32.44 at 4,912.04
348 -2 * Volume NZ$53 million. Futures +15 at 1,183
740 -2 * Other movers -23 +7
Late buying nudged New Zealand shares into positive territory on Monday, the eve of an expected announcement by the New Zealand First party of its choice of coalition partner.
The NZSE-40 capital index closed 0.25 points higher at 2,361.17 as strength in Telecom, Carter Holt Harvey and Fletcher Building outweighed the negative 14-point impact of stocks going ex-dividend.
Telecom closed two cents lower at NZ$7.40 after going ex a 9.5 cent dividend.

Casino operator Sky City continued its losing streak, shedding eight cents to $7.70 on top of Friday's 44-point drop after news of lower visitor numbers and a budget over-run on its Auckland Sky Tower.
Fashion retailer Hallenstein Glasson ended 22 lower at $2.73 after going 12 cents ex-dividend.

Hallenstein last week said it expected a lower first half result, and Jim Patterson at First NZ Capital said that brokerage had lowered its 1997 full year forecast for the group to NZ$11.5 million from $17.3 million.

Patterson said he saw some "short-term negativity" if nationalist NZ First chose Labour instead of the conservative National Party as its coalition ally, with prospects for higher government spending and looser monetary policy.

Another broker said the market feared the influence of the left-wing Alliance in any Labour-led coalition, but Phil Hardie Boys at BZW said he expected any selling on new of such a government to be relatively short-lived.
NZ First MPs meet on Tuesday to decide between Labour and National, ending a two-month hiatus since a general election.
